PCE.title: PyTorch CrossEntropyLoss
PCE.verification: Official versioned page read using web; no original HTML snapshot hash claimed

items.INDEX: Definition of unreduced class-index loss and indicator for ignored targets; API documentation loss formula.
items.REDUCE: Class-index mean divides by summed target-class weights of non-ignored rows; sum is sum of row losses; none returns row losses.
items.PROB: Probability-target loss weights each class term; mean divides by N.
items.IGNORE: Ignore index may lie outside the class range; ignored rows do not contribute input gradient; class-index targets only.
items.SMOOTH: Targets are mixed with the uniform class distribution.
items.SHAPE: Target/index/probability shapes and reduction output shape; probability constraints are caller responsibilities.

PCE.snapshot_check: items INDEX (unreduced class-index formula with w_{y_n} and the ignore indicator), REDUCE (mean divides by the sum of w_{y_n} over non-ignored rows; sum; none), PROB (l_n = -sum_c w_c log softmax_c y_{n,c}; mean divides by N), IGNORE (index may lie outside [0,C); no input-gradient contribution; class indices only), SMOOTH (mixture with the uniform distribution, prose only) and SHAPE found in the archived text; no conflict with the reviewed clauses. Weighted smoothing is not given by a formula, consistent with decision CE.R_A needing a binding. Checked by the spec v3 author (Claude), not an external review.

PAW.title: PyTorch AdamW
PAW.verification: Official versioned algorithm box read using web; no original HTML snapshot hash claimed

items.DECAY: Decay old parameter before adaptive parameter update; weight decay is not added to moments.
items.MOMENTS: m uses beta1 and gradient; v uses beta2 and gradient squared.
items.CORRECTION: Current step t appears in 1-beta**t; amsgrad=False uses the current second moment.
items.UPDATE: Subtract lr*m_hat/(sqrt(v_hat)+eps); eps is outside sqrt.
items.NONE: The zero_grad note distinguishes None (step skipped) from a zero gradient (full step).

No conflict with the reviewed clauses. Checked by the spec v3 author (Claude), not an external review.

R1 (fixed kernel size) is kept as the tail reading for comparison; the 2.10 AvgPool3d text still calls the default divisor kernel_size (tension); a difference caused only by the overhang divisor is not by itself a confirmed bug. items.POOL_A2: POOL-A2: for finite windows with an actual maximum, the forward index must belong to the set of tied maximisers; first or last is not imposed. Strict ordinary-derivative scoring is limited to a unique maximum; at ties a set check applies: g_i = v*alpha_i with alpha zero outside the tie set, nonnegative on it and summing to 1. Single-member routing and even splitting are not judged against each other; (2,-1) is not legal. Only if a task additionally declares that backward uses the returned indices is the routing checked per call.
items.POOL_A3: POOL-A3: R_prop is the project's NaN diagnostic profile; only NaNs that actually participate in the current window propagate. Undocumented NaN behaviour does not enter the main correctness rate; R_ignore may be listed separately and is not an error merely for not propagating. All-NaN and geometrically empty windows are recorded separately.
items.POOL_A5: POOL-A5: when a window samples no real input, by the negative-infinity padding the output is -inf and the argmax set over real inputs is empty; the returned index is not required to belong to the empty set; there is no gradient routing to real inputs. An empty set caused by NaN filtering is a different case.
items.IDX_A3: IDX-A3: R_prop is the project's NaN diagnostic profile for amax/amin, applied only to values that actually take part in the reduction (with include_self=False the old self does not take part; positions not updated stay unchanged).

items.ACC_A1: ACC-A1: if the whole accumulation window has no valid token the token-average target is undefined (skip/zero/NaN conventions are recorded, not judged as math bugs); an individual empty micro-batch with a positive window total keeps the target defined, contributing 0; global sum over global count, never the mean of micro-batch means.

items.POOL_A0: POOL-A0: AvgPool1d and AvgPool3d documentation each give formula, padding, ceil window start and per-dimension correction, so the basic rules have a basis for every dimensionality; the only tension is the AvgPool3d divisor_override text calling the default divisor kernel_size.

items.PADDING: padding_idx: entries at padding_idx do not contribute to the gradient, and the embedding vector at padding_idx is excluded from the reduction; example: a bag consisting only of padding_idx entries gives zeros with mode='sum'.
items.MAX_OPTS: scale_grad_by_freq and sparse are not supported when mode='max'.
items.MAX_NORM: max_norm: each embedding vector with norm larger than max_norm is renormalized to have norm max_norm (weight modified in place).

items.EQUIV: For bags of constant length, no per_sample_weights, no indices equal to padding_idx and 2D inputs, mode='sum' is equivalent to Embedding followed by torch.sum(dim=1), mode='mean' to torch.mean(dim=1), mode='max' to torch.max(dim=1).
items.PSW: per_sample_weights scale the output of the Embedding before the weighted reduction; with per_sample_weights the only supported mode is 'sum', which computes a weighted sum.
items.MODES: 'sum' computes the weighted sum taking per_sample_weights into consideration, 'mean' computes the average of the values in the bag, 'max' computes the max value over each bag.
items.PADDING: padding_idx entries do not contribute to the gradient and the embedding vector at padding_idx is excluded from the reduction.

items.EMB_RENORM: embedding: if max_norm is not None, _no_grad_embedding_renorm_(weight, input, max_norm, norm_type) (equivalent to embedding_renorm_ under torch.no_grad()) runs before torch.embedding(weight, input, padding_idx, scale_grad_by_freq, sparse).
items.EMB_PADDING: embedding: a positive padding_idx must be < weight.size(0); a negative one must be >= -weight.size(0) and is replaced by weight.size(0) + padding_idx; None becomes -1.
items.BAG_CHECKS: embedding_bag: per_sample_weights must have the size of input; mode must be sum, mean or max; mode max raises for scale_grad_by_freq; per_sample_weights is only supported for mode='sum'; with max_norm, _no_grad_embedding_renorm_(weight, input, ...) runs first.

items.MATH: math_attention (eager implementation): key and value repeat_interleave'd over heads for GQA; scores = query @ key^T, then scores * scale; post_mod_scores = score_mod(scores, b, h, m, n) where mask_mod(b, h, m, n) is True and -inf elsewhere; output = _safe_softmax(post_mod_scores, dim=-1) @ value.
items.LSE_MASKED: logsumexp of post_mod_scores, set to -inf for fully masked rows, is returned divided by log(2) because the kernel works in ln2 space and the top-level op converts back.

items.LSE: flex_attention returns lse_scaled = lse * ln2 (ln2 = math.log(2.0)) of the internal log-sum-exp, i.e. the returned lse is in natural log units.

items.SAFE_SOFTMAX: _safe_softmax(self, dim): out = softmax(self, dim); rows in which every element is -inf (isneginf, all along dim) are set to 0.
items.MATH: _scaled_dot_product_attention_math: with is_causal the mask is ones(L, S).tril() (explicit attn_mask not allowed); with enable_gqa key/value are repeat_interleave'd by Hq/H along dim -3; attn = (scaled q) @ (scaled k)^T plus the mask; attn = _safe_softmax(attn, -1); output attn @ value.

items.FORWARD: embedding: weight.index_select(0, indices) reshaped to the index shape followed by the embedding dimension.
items.RENORM: embedding_renorm_cpu_: for each distinct index, norm = row.norm(norm_type); if norm > max_norm, row *= max_norm / (norm + 1e-7).
items.DENSE_BWD: embedding_dense_backward_cpu: grad_weight[k] += grad[i] * scale for every position i whose index k != padding_idx; scale = 1/counts[k] (number of occurrences of k in indices) when scale_grad_by_freq, else 1.

items.OFFSETS: offsets[0] has to be 0 (the first sequence in the mini-batch starts at position 0).
items.MAX: mode max (CPU): indices are visited in bag order; padding_idx entries are skipped (bag_size decremented); an element replaces the current value when it is the first of the bag or strictly greater (weight_item > current_item), and max_indices records its word index.
items.MEAN: mode mean multiplies the bag sum by 1 / bag_size (bag_size excluding padding entries).

items.CAUSAL_BR: If causal=True, the causal mask is aligned to the bottom right corner of the attention matrix: seqlen_q=2, seqlen_k=5 gives rows 1 1 1 1 0 / 1 1 1 1 1; seqlen_q=5, seqlen_k=2 gives rows 0 0 / 0 0 / 0 0 / 1 0 / 1 1.
items.EMPTY_ROW: If the row of the mask is all zero, the output will be zero.
items.WINDOW: If window_size != (-1, -1), query at position i attends only to keys in [i + seqlen_k - seqlen_q - window_size[0], i + seqlen_k - seqlen_q + window_size[1]] inclusive; -1 means infinite context window.
items.GQA: MQA/GQA: the number of heads in Q must be divisible by the number of heads in KV; with 6 Q heads and 2 KV heads, Q heads 0, 1, 2 attend KV head 0 and Q heads 3, 4, 5 attend KV head 1.
items.VARLEN: flash_attn_varlen_func: cu_seqlens_q / cu_seqlens_k of shape (batch_size + 1,) are the cumulative sequence lengths of the sequences in the batch, used to index into the packed q and kv.
items.SOFTCAP: softcap: float; anything > 0 activates softcapping attention.
items.SCALE: softmax_scale: the scaling of QK^T before applying softmax; default 1 / sqrt(headdim).
items.LSE: softmax_lse: the logsumexp of each row of the matrix QK^T * scaling (the log of the softmax normalization factor).

items.FWD: attention(q, k, v, causal, sm_scale): the forward kernel uses qk_scale = sm_scale * 1.44269504 (1/log(2)) with exp2, writes o = acc / l_i and M = m_i + log2(l_i) per query row.
items.CAUSAL: causal=True: blocks on the diagonal are masked with offs_m >= start_n + offs_n (query i attends keys j <= i); query and key share the length N_CTX.
items.BWD: backward computes dq, dk, dv from q, k, v, o, do and M; the test is parametrized with causal=[True] only, with the comment 'FIXME: Non-causal tests do not pass at the moment.'
items.TEST_REF: test reference: p = q @ k^T * sm_scale, -inf where tril(ones(N_CTX, N_CTX)) == 0 when causal, softmax, then p @ v.

VLLM_UA.title: vLLM main 51eeb0c vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py
VLLM_UA.version: 51eeb0c (2026-10-05; same code in v0.24.0-v0.31.0 per 4_bugs_cases B013)

items.SIGNATURE: unified_attention(q, k, v, out, cu_seqlens_q, max_seqlen_q, seqused_k, max_seqlen_k, softmax_scale, causal, window_size, block_table, softcap, ...); q is (num_tokens, num_query_heads, head_size), k and v are the paged caches.
items.BLOCK_TABLE: key/value of position seq_offset of a sequence are read at physical block block_table[seq, seq_offset // BLOCK_SIZE], slot seq_offset % BLOCK_SIZE, kv head kv_head_idx.
items.POSITIONS: context_len = seq_len - cur_batch_query_len; query_abs_pos = context_len + query_pos (the query tokens are the last query_len positions of the sequence).
items.GQA: query head = kv_head_idx * num_queries_per_kv + offs_m % num_queries_per_kv with num_queries_per_kv = num_query_heads // num_kv_heads.
items.ORDER: S = softmax_scale * (Q K); softcap applied when softcap > 0; then S = -inf outside the query and KV masks; then the online softmax.
items.WINDOW_ARG: the kernel receives SLIDING_WINDOW = 1 + window_size[0]; window_size[1] is not passed.
items.V_MASK: with SLIDING_WINDOW, V rows are zeroed unless dist < SLIDING_WINDOW (causal) or (dist < SLIDING_WINDOW) & (dist > -SLIDING_WINDOW) (non-causal), dist = context_len + qpos_lo - seq_offset with qpos_lo the first query position of the query block.

items.KV_MASK: compute_kv_seq_mask: causal: key position <= query_abs_pos; non-causal: key position < seq_len; sliding window: (query_abs_pos - key) < SLIDING_WINDOW and, when not causal, also (key - query_abs_pos) < SLIDING_WINDOW.
items.SOFTCAP: apply_softcap(S, x) = x * tanh(S / x), computed as x * (1 - 2 / (exp(2 S / x) + 1)).

items.ROTATE_HALF: rotate_half(x) = cat(-x2, x1) with x1 = x[..., :d/2] and x2 = x[..., d/2:].
items.APPLY: apply_rotary_pos_emb: q_embed = q * cos + rotate_half(q) * sin (same for k).
items.TABLES: LlamaRotaryEmbedding: freqs = inv_freq times position_ids; emb = cat(freqs, freqs); cos = emb.cos() * attention_scaling, sin = emb.sin() * attention_scaling.
items.REPEAT_KV: repeat_kv is the equivalent of torch.repeat_interleave(x, dim=1, repeats=n_rep) from key/value heads to attention heads.

items.DEFAULT: _compute_default_rope_parameters: dim = int(head_dim * partial_rotary_factor); inv_freq = 1 / (base ** (arange(0, dim, 2) / dim)); attention_factor = 1.0.
items.LINEAR: _compute_linear_scaling_rope_parameters: the default inv_freq divided by rope_scaling['factor'] (noted as equivalent to scaling the position ids).

items.PARTIAL: apply_rotary_pos_emb: rotary_dim = cos.shape[-1]; q_rot = q[..., :rotary_dim], q_pass = q[..., rotary_dim:]; q_embed = cat(q_rot * cos + rotate_half(q_rot) * sin, q_pass).

items.HALF: the rotary embedding returns emb = freqs (not duplicated); _apply_rotary_emb: first_half, second_half = chunk(x, 2); first_ = first_half * cos - second_half * sin; second_ = second_half * cos + first_half * sin; cat(first_, second_).

items.EVERY_TWO: rotate_every_two maps the pairs (x[2i], x[2i+1]) to (-x[2i+1], x[2i]); apply_rotary_pos_emb repeat_interleaves sin and cos by 2 and returns x * cos + rotate_every_two(x) * sin; inv_freq = 1 / (10000 ** (arange(0, dim, 2) / dim)).

items.ROUTER: MixtralSparseMoeBlock: routing_weights = softmax(router_logits, dim=1); routing_weights, selected_experts = topk(routing_weights, top_k); routing_weights /= routing_weights.sum(-1, keepdim=True).
items.AUX: load_balancing_loss_func (Switch Transformer eqs. 4-6): expert_mask = one_hot(top-k selected experts); tokens_per_expert = mean over tokens of expert_mask (per top-k slot and expert); router_prob_per_expert = mean over tokens of the softmax probabilities; loss = num_experts * sum(tokens_per_expert * router_prob_per_expert).

items.SOFTCAP: eager_attention_forward: attn_weights = q @ k^T * scaling; with softcap, attn_weights = tanh(attn_weights / softcap) * softcap; then the attention mask is added and softmax applied.

items.FLATTEN: DataCollatorWithFlattening concatenates the mini batch into one sequence; position_ids += list(range(len(input_ids))) per example (restarting at 0); optional cu_seq_lens (cumulative lengths) and seq_idx (index of the sequence of each token).

items.HF: LigerRopeFunction implements the HuggingFace Llama & Mistral version of RoPE; q (bsz, n_q_head, seq_len, head_dim), k (bsz, n_kv_head, seq_len, head_dim), cos and sin (1 or bsz, seq_len, head_dim).
items.LEFT_HALF: the kernel loads only the left half of cos and sin (offsets < head_dim / 2) because 'the right half is just a clone of the left half'; y1 = x1 * cos - x2 * sin, y2 = x2 * cos + x1 * sin with x1, x2 the two halves of the head.
items.BWD: backward pass: dx1 = dy1 * cos + dy2 * sin, dx2 = dy2 * cos - dy1 * sin.

ROFORMER.title: Su et al., RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding (arXiv:2104.09864, ar5iv HTML rendering)

items.ROTARY: eq. (15): the rotary matrix R^d_{Theta,m} is block diagonal with 2x2 blocks [[cos m theta_i, -sin m theta_i], [sin m theta_i, cos m theta_i]] acting on (x_{2i-1}, x_{2i}), i = 1..d/2.
items.RELATIVE: eq. (16): q_m^T k_n = (R_m W_q x_m)^T (R_n W_k x_n) = x^T W_q R_{n-m} W_k x_n with R_{n-m} = R_m^T R_n; R is orthogonal.
items.EFFICIENT: eq. (34): R x = x (elementwise) (cos m theta_1, cos m theta_1, cos m theta_2, cos m theta_2, ...) + (-x_2, x_1, -x_4, x_3, ...) (elementwise) (sin m theta_1, sin m theta_1, ...).

items.ROUTER: eq. (1): router logits h(x) = W_r x are normalized by a softmax over the N experts, gate value p_i(x) = e^{h(x)_i} / sum_j e^{h(x)_j}.
items.COMBINE: eq. (2): y = sum over the selected top-k set T of p_i(x) E_i(x); the Switch layer routes to a single expert (k = 1).
items.CAPACITY: expert capacity = (tokens per batch / number of experts) x capacity factor; tokens routed to an expert beyond its capacity are dropped: computation is skipped and the representation is passed to the next layer through the residual connection.
items.AUX: eq. (4) loss = alpha * N * sum_i f_i * P_i; eq. (5) f_i = (1/T) sum_x 1{argmax p(x) = i}, the fraction of tokens dispatched to expert i; eq. (6) P_i = (1/T) sum_x p_i(x).
items.CODE: appendix router code: top-1 expert_index and expert_gate; aux_loss = load_balance_loss(router_probs, expert_mask) computed from the top-1 mask before capacity masking; position_in_expert = cumsum of expert_mask over the tokens; expert_mask kept only where position_in_expert is less than expert_capacity; the gate of masked tokens is zeroed.
